questions.prompt: Which term describes the purposeful action that drives conflict and change in a play or performance?
options: Dramatic action
Ticket pricing
Costume storage
Stage cleaning
questions.correctAnswer: Dramatic action
questions.explanation: Dramatic action is what characters do to pursue objectives and create conflict, tension, and development.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify dramatic action as the engine of scripted and devised performance.

questions.prompt: In actor preparation, what does a character objective state?
options: What the character wants in a scene
Where tickets will be sold
How many lights are in the hall
Which camera battery is charged
questions.correctAnswer: What the character wants in a scene
questions.explanation: A character objective gives the actor a playable intention that shapes voice, movement, and interaction.
questions.learningOutcome: Recall how objectives guide character performance choices.

questions.prompt: Which performance principle means actors work together with shared timing, focus, and responsibility?
options: Ensemble
Monopoly
Spot metering
Box office
questions.correctAnswer: Ensemble
questions.explanation: Ensemble work depends on listening, trust, shared rhythm, and support among performers.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise ensemble as a foundation of collaborative performance.

questions.prompt: What does blocking record in a theatre rehearsal script?
options: Planned actor movement and positions on stage
The price of each seat
The colour of the school gate
The number of audience claps
questions.correctAnswer: Planned actor movement and positions on stage
questions.explanation: Blocking notes help performers and directors repeat clear, safe, and meaningful stage movement.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify blocking as planned movement and placement in performance space.

questions.prompt: In dance composition, what is a movement motif?
options: A short movement idea that can be repeated and developed
A theatre ticket receipt
A camera lens cap
A random backstage noise
questions.correctAnswer: A short movement idea that can be repeated and developed
questions.explanation: A motif gives choreography a recognisable idea that can be varied through space, time, energy, and relationships.
questions.learningOutcome: Define movement motif as a building block of choreography.

questions.prompt: Which dance element refers to the quality or force of movement, such as sharp, sustained, heavy, or light?
options: Energy
Programme
Costume rack
Dialogue
questions.correctAnswer: Energy
questions.explanation: Energy describes how movement is performed and helps communicate mood, intention, and style.
questions.learningOutcome: Recall energy as an element used to shape expressive movement.

questions.prompt: In a screenplay, what is the main purpose of a scene heading such as INT. CLASSROOM - DAY?
options: It states location and time for filming the scene
It lists audience reactions after the show
It explains ticket discounts
It names the costume designer only
questions.correctAnswer: It states location and time for filming the scene
questions.explanation: A scene heading tells the production team where and when the action takes place.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the function of scene headings in screenwriting.

questions.prompt: Which film term means keeping props, costume, action, and eyelines consistent across shots?
options: Continuity
Improvisation
Curtain call
Mime
questions.correctAnswer: Continuity
questions.explanation: Continuity helps separate shots appear as one believable flow of action when edited together.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise continuity as consistency across filmed shots.

questions.prompt: Who usually calls lighting, sound, entrance, and scene-change cues during a live performance?
options: Stage manager
Audience usher
Poster designer
Ticket buyer
questions.correctAnswer: Stage manager
questions.explanation: The stage manager coordinates cues and backstage communication so the performance runs in sequence.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the cue-calling responsibility of the stage manager.

questions.prompt: What is dramaturgical research used for before rehearsing a play?
options: Understanding context, sources, themes, and performance possibilities
Replacing all rehearsal with ticket sales
Choosing snacks for the interval
Counting chairs in the staffroom
questions.correctAnswer: Understanding context, sources, themes, and performance possibilities
questions.explanation: Dramaturgical research informs interpretation by connecting the script to history, culture, form, and meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Recall the purpose of dramaturgical research in performance preparation.

questions.prompt: Which staging arrangement places the audience mainly in front of the performers, as if viewing through a frame?
options: Proscenium stage
Arena stage
Promenade performance
Theatre-in-the-round
questions.correctAnswer: Proscenium stage
questions.explanation: A proscenium arrangement frames the action from one principal audience direction.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify a proscenium stage configuration.

questions.prompt: What does a cue sheet usually record for a production?
options: The order and timing of sound, lighting, projection, or scene-change cues
The personal marks of every performer
The price of fabric in the market
The biography of every audience member
questions.correctAnswer: The order and timing of sound, lighting, projection, or scene-change cues
questions.explanation: A cue sheet supports accurate technical operation by listing when each cue happens.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify cue sheets as technical production documents.

questions.prompt: Which word describes a reasoned judgement of a performance using evidence from acting, design, structure, or audience response?
options: Critique
Casting call
Warm-up
Prop list
questions.correctAnswer: Critique
questions.explanation: A critique evaluates performance choices with specific evidence rather than unsupported opinion.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise critique as evidence-based performance judgement.

questions.prompt: Which ethical requirement should be obtained before recording a person's performance or interview for a film project?
options: Informed consent
Random applause
Silent blocking
Unmarked costume
questions.correctAnswer: Informed consent
questions.explanation: Informed consent shows that a participant understands and agrees to being recorded and to the intended use.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify consent as an ethical requirement in recorded performance work.

questions.prompt: Which production document estimates income and expenditure for a performance event?
options: Budget
Storyboard
Monologue
Casting slate
questions.correctAnswer: Budget
questions.explanation: A budget helps the production team plan resources, avoid waste, and track financial decisions.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify a budget as a financial planning tool for performance production.

questions.prompt: Why is subtext important when performing dialogue?
options: It helps actors communicate hidden meanings beneath spoken words
It makes every line louder than necessary
It removes the need for listening
It turns a script into a poster
questions.correctAnswer: It helps actors communicate hidden meanings beneath spoken words
questions.explanation: Subtext gives depth to dialogue because characters often imply feelings or motives rather than state them directly.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how subtext enriches character performance.

questions.prompt: Why should a choreographer vary levels, directions, and formations in a group dance?
options: To create visual interest and clarify relationships in space
To stop dancers from hearing the music
To make all movement identical
To hide the main idea from the audience
questions.correctAnswer: To create visual interest and clarify relationships in space
questions.explanation: Spatial variation helps the audience follow focus, contrast, pattern, and relationships within the dance.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how spatial choices support choreographic meaning.

questions.prompt: How does a beat change help an actor shape a scene?
options: It marks a shift in thought, tactic, emotion, or relationship
It guarantees a costume change
It replaces all stage directions
It prevents pauses from having meaning
questions.correctAnswer: It marks a shift in thought, tactic, emotion, or relationship
questions.explanation: Recognising beat changes helps actors adjust pace, focus, breath, and intention at key moments.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the function of beat changes in scene performance.

questions.prompt: Why is a storyboard useful before shooting a short film?
options: It plans visual sequence, framing, and shot order before filming
It replaces the need for sound recording
It records audience ticket numbers
It guarantees actors will never miss lines
questions.correctAnswer: It plans visual sequence, framing, and shot order before filming
questions.explanation: A storyboard turns script action into planned images, helping the crew shoot efficiently and coherently.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how storyboards support film planning.

questions.prompt: Why should a director consider sightlines when staging a performance?
options: So important action remains visible to the audience
So actors can ignore voice projection
So costumes can be stored on stage
So the story can be hidden
questions.correctAnswer: So important action remains visible to the audience
questions.explanation: Good sightlines allow the audience to see key performers, gestures, set pieces, and stage pictures clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why sightlines matter in staging choices.

questions.prompt: Why is warm-up important before voice and movement rehearsal?
options: It prepares the body and voice for expressive, safer performance work
It eliminates the need for rehearsal discipline
It makes performers shout automatically
It replaces character analysis
questions.correctAnswer: It prepares the body and voice for expressive, safer performance work
questions.explanation: Warm-ups increase focus, breath support, flexibility, coordination, and readiness while reducing strain.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the value of vocal and physical warm-ups before performance.

questions.prompt: How does contrast strengthen a stage picture?
options: It makes differences in level, distance, direction, or grouping communicate focus and tension
It forces every actor to stand in a straight line
It removes meaning from performer placement
It prevents audience attention
questions.correctAnswer: It makes differences in level, distance, direction, or grouping communicate focus and tension
questions.explanation: Contrasting visual choices can reveal power, conflict, isolation, unity, or change without extra dialogue.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how visual contrast supports stage composition.

questions.prompt: Why is room tone recorded during a film shoot?
options: To make sound edits smoother by capturing the natural background sound
To replace all dialogue with silence
To measure the width of the location
To select dance costumes
questions.correctAnswer: To make sound edits smoother by capturing the natural background sound
questions.explanation: Room tone gives editors consistent ambient sound to bridge cuts and avoid unnatural silence.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of recording room tone for film editing.

questions.prompt: Why should performers avoid turning their backs to the audience for long periods unless it is intentional?
options: It can reduce vocal clarity, facial expression, and audience connection
It always improves projection
It makes blocking easier to read
It guarantees stronger characterisation
questions.correctAnswer: It can reduce vocal clarity, facial expression, and audience connection
questions.explanation: Audience communication depends on visibility, audibility, and purposeful orientation in the performance space.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how performer orientation affects audience reception.

questions.prompt: How does foreshadowing help a dramatic script?
options: It plants clues that prepare later events while keeping interest alive
It removes every surprise from the story
It forces all characters to speak in riddles
It replaces conflict with description
questions.correctAnswer: It plants clues that prepare later events while keeping interest alive
questions.explanation: Foreshadowing links earlier details to later outcomes, making plot development feel earned.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of foreshadowing in dramatic structure.

questions.prompt: Why should a production team credit a community storyteller when adapting an oral narrative?
options: It respects authorship, cultural knowledge, and source contribution
It stops the performers from being creative
It hides where the story came from
It makes audience feedback impossible
questions.correctAnswer: It respects authorship, cultural knowledge, and source contribution
questions.explanation: Attribution recognises the people and communities whose knowledge informs the performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain ethical attribution when adapting community-sourced performance material.

questions.prompt: Why is rehearsal etiquette important in a Grade 12 production process?
options: It supports punctuality, respect, focus, safety, and reliable collaboration
It allows performers to ignore deadlines
It makes directors unnecessary
It turns feedback into personal attack
questions.correctAnswer: It supports punctuality, respect, focus, safety, and reliable collaboration
questions.explanation: Professional habits make rehearsal more efficient and protect the quality of group work.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain rehearsal etiquette as part of production responsibility.

questions.prompt: How does a reaction shot support film storytelling?
options: It shows how a character responds to action, information, or another person
It proves editing is unnecessary
It removes emotion from the scene
It changes a stage play into a budget
questions.correctAnswer: It shows how a character responds to action, information, or another person
questions.explanation: Reaction shots help viewers understand relationships, consequences, and inner response.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how reaction shots communicate character response.

questions.prompt: Why is feedback stronger when it refers to specific performance evidence?
options: It becomes clearer, fairer, and easier for performers to use
It avoids discussing what happened on stage
It rewards only the loudest opinion
It prevents revision after rehearsal
questions.correctAnswer: It becomes clearer, fairer, and easier for performers to use
questions.explanation: Evidence-based feedback links comments to observable choices such as pace, focus, gesture, voice, or design.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the value of specific evidence in performance critique.

questions.prompt: Why should set pieces and props be checked before a live presentation?
options: To confirm they are safe, available, functional, and correctly placed
To make actors skip entrances
To increase backstage confusion
To replace the stage manager's role
questions.correctAnswer: To confirm they are safe, available, functional, and correctly placed
questions.explanation: Pre-show checks reduce risk, delays, broken business, and avoidable performance interruptions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why pre-show prop and set checks support production readiness.

questions.prompt: Why is an audition notice expected to give roles, dates, venue, preparation task, and contact details?
options: It allows interested performers to prepare and attend fairly
It hides useful information from learners
It prevents casting decisions from being organised
It replaces rehearsal planning
questions.correctAnswer: It allows interested performers to prepare and attend fairly
questions.explanation: Clear audition communication supports fairness, planning, and informed participation.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain clear communication requirements for audition planning.

questions.prompt: How can pacing influence audience engagement in a scene?
options: It controls rhythm, tension, emphasis, and the audience's sense of progression
It makes all scenes the same length
It removes the need for objectives
It ensures dialogue is always rushed
questions.correctAnswer: It controls rhythm, tension, emphasis, and the audience's sense of progression
questions.explanation: Varied pacing helps important moments land and prevents the performance from feeling flat or unclear.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how pace shapes dramatic communication.

questions.prompt: Why should costume choices support character, setting, movement, and safety?
options: Costume must communicate meaning while allowing performers to move safely
Costume is only decoration with no performance function
Every performer must wear identical clothing
Costume should hide all character relationships
questions.correctAnswer: Costume must communicate meaning while allowing performers to move safely
questions.explanation: Effective costume design balances visual storytelling, practical movement, cultural fit, and performer safety.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how costume contributes to performance meaning and practicality.

questions.prompt: Why should a devised performance have a clear through-line?
options: It connects scenes and choices around a central idea or journey
It makes every scene unrelated
It prevents performers from using movement
It turns rehearsal into ticket counting
questions.correctAnswer: It connects scenes and choices around a central idea or journey
questions.explanation: A through-line helps audiences follow the development of meaning across devised material.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how a through-line gives unity to devised performance.

questions.prompt: How does a low-angle camera shot often affect the audience's reading of a character?
options: It can make the character appear powerful, dominant, or significant
It always makes the character look smaller
It removes all visual meaning
It turns the shot into a sound cue
questions.correctAnswer: It can make the character appear powerful, dominant, or significant
questions.explanation: Camera angle changes perspective, so looking up at a character can suggest status or authority.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how camera angle can shape character interpretation.

questions.prompt: Why is cultural sensitivity important when presenting dances or stories from a community?
options: It avoids misrepresentation and respects context, meaning, and ownership
It encourages mocking community practices
It means no research is needed
It requires every performance to be silent
questions.correctAnswer: It avoids misrepresentation and respects context, meaning, and ownership
questions.explanation: Responsible performance considers source context and avoids reducing cultural material to inaccurate display.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why cultural sensitivity matters in performance creation.

questions.prompt: Why is a release form useful for a school documentary interview?
options: It records permission and clarifies how footage may be used
It improves camera focus automatically
It replaces respectful questioning
It removes the need for accurate editing
questions.correctAnswer: It records permission and clarifies how footage may be used
questions.explanation: A release form documents consent and protects both participants and producers.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of release forms in responsible documentary production.

questions.prompt: Why might a director ask actors to improvise before returning to a scripted scene?
options: To explore objectives, relationships, and natural responses before refining text
To avoid learning the scene forever
To delete the script's conflict
To replace rehearsal notes with jokes
questions.correctAnswer: To explore objectives, relationships, and natural responses before refining text
questions.explanation: Improvisation can reveal truthful behaviour and clarify performance choices within the written scene.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how improvisation can deepen scripted performance.

questions.prompt: How does lighting contribute to mood in a performance?
options: Intensity, angle, colour, and contrast can guide emotional atmosphere and focus
Lighting only helps the audience find seats
Lighting has no effect once dialogue begins
All moods require the same bright wash
questions.correctAnswer: Intensity, angle, colour, and contrast can guide emotional atmosphere and focus
questions.explanation: Lighting choices can signal time, tension, warmth, danger, isolation, or attention while keeping action visible.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how lighting choices shape audience interpretation.

questions.prompt: Why should a production reflection include what worked, what failed, and what should change next time?
options: It turns experience into practical learning for future performance work
It is only a way to blame performers
It replaces audience communication
It makes future planning unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: It turns experience into practical learning for future performance work
questions.explanation: Reflection helps learners connect evidence from process and performance to improvement decisions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how production reflection supports continuous improvement.

questions.prompt: A Grade 12 group is staging a scene in a hall with audience on three sides. Which blocking choice is best?
options: Rotate focus and keep key action visible from multiple audience angles
Face every performer permanently to one wall
Place the climax behind a tall set piece
Keep all actors seated with backs turned
questions.correctAnswer: Rotate focus and keep key action visible from multiple audience angles
questions.explanation: Three-sided staging requires shared visibility, open body orientation, and flexible stage pictures.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply blocking principles to a thrust or three-sided performance space.

questions.prompt: A choreographer wants to develop a motif without losing its identity. Which revision is strongest?
options: Repeat the motif with changes in level, tempo, direction, and group relationships
Replace the motif with unrelated steps every time
Stop the music whenever the motif appears
Ask dancers to perform random movements
questions.correctAnswer: Repeat the motif with changes in level, tempo, direction, and group relationships
questions.explanation: Development keeps the core idea recognisable while creating variety and progression.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply choreographic devices to develop a movement motif.

questions.prompt: A scene requires a character to hide fear while speaking politely. Which actor choice best communicates this?
options: Use controlled speech with small hesitations, tense posture, and guarded eye contact
Shout every line with no physical control
Smile broadly with relaxed movement throughout
Ignore the other actor's presence
questions.correctAnswer: Use controlled speech with small hesitations, tense posture, and guarded eye contact
questions.explanation: Contrasting polite words with restrained physical tension can reveal fear through subtext.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply vocal and physical choices to reveal subtext.

questions.prompt: A film crew wants to show two learners sitting opposite each other in conversation. Which filming rule helps preserve clear screen direction?
options: Keep the camera on one side of the action line unless a crossing is motivated
Move the camera randomly around the table for every shot
Reverse every eyeline without planning
Film only the ceiling during dialogue
questions.correctAnswer: Keep the camera on one side of the action line unless a crossing is motivated
questions.explanation: The 180-degree guideline helps viewers understand where characters are in relation to one another.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply screen direction principles to a dialogue scene.

questions.prompt: A group wants to dramatise a newspaper report about water shortage. Which choice makes it theatrical rather than just informational?
options: Create characters with conflicting needs and decisions affected by the shortage
Read the full report aloud without interaction
List statistics while standing still for ten minutes
Remove all human consequences from the event
questions.correctAnswer: Create characters with conflicting needs and decisions affected by the shortage
questions.explanation: Drama emerges when information is embodied in characters, conflict, choices, and consequences.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply dramatic transformation to factual material.

questions.prompt: A dancer keeps arriving late to group rehearsal and misses spacing changes. Which production response is most appropriate?
options: Address rehearsal responsibility, update the dancer, and confirm attendance expectations
Remove all spacing from the choreography
Let the group guess formations during performance
Punish the whole cast by cancelling every rehearsal note
questions.correctAnswer: Address rehearsal responsibility, update the dancer, and confirm attendance expectations
questions.explanation: Reliable participation and clear communication protect group quality while allowing practical correction.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply professional rehearsal conduct to ensemble work.

questions.prompt: A script's final scene feels abrupt because the central conflict is not answered. Which revision best strengthens the ending?
options: Add a final choice or consequence that resolves or reframes the main conflict
Repeat the opening argument exactly
Add unrelated dancing after the last line
Remove the strongest earlier conflict
questions.correctAnswer: Add a final choice or consequence that resolves or reframes the main conflict
questions.explanation: An ending should show how the central dramatic pressure lands for characters and audience.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply revision strategies to strengthen dramatic resolution.

questions.prompt: A school short film has dialogue near a busy road. Which sound choice best improves clarity?
options: Place a microphone close to the speakers and choose a quieter angle or time
Record from far away because the camera can see the actors
Cover the microphone completely with thick cloth
Ignore the dialogue and fix everything with louder music
questions.correctAnswer: Place a microphone close to the speakers and choose a quieter angle or time
questions.explanation: Good production sound depends on close placement, controlled noise, and clear speech capture.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply practical sound recording choices for location filming.

questions.prompt: A class performance includes a scene about grief. Which rehearsal practice is most responsible?
options: Set respectful boundaries, clarify purpose, and support performers during rehearsal
Force performers to share personal trauma for realism
Make the topic a joke to reduce seriousness
Rehearse emotional scenes without teacher oversight
questions.correctAnswer: Set respectful boundaries, clarify purpose, and support performers during rehearsal
questions.explanation: Sensitive content requires care, consent, supervision, and attention to learner wellbeing.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply ethical rehearsal practice for sensitive themes.

questions.prompt: A group wants to use a popular song under their original film scene. What is the most responsible decision?
options: Use original, licensed, or permission-cleared music that supports the scene
Use the song without checking rights because it is well known
Make the music so loud that dialogue cannot be heard
Credit the artist only if the film wins a prize
questions.correctAnswer: Use original, licensed, or permission-cleared music that supports the scene
questions.explanation: Responsible sound design respects intellectual property and ensures music serves the story.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply ethical criteria when selecting music for media performance.

questions.prompt: A performer must project in a large hall without shouting. Which technique should they use?
options: Support breath, articulate clearly, and direct sound toward the audience
Tighten the throat and force every word
Speak faster so words reach the back
Turn away from the audience while speaking
questions.correctAnswer: Support breath, articulate clearly, and direct sound toward the audience
questions.explanation: Healthy projection combines breath support, resonance, articulation, and audience awareness.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe vocal techniques for live performance spaces.

questions.prompt: A director wants to show a character becoming isolated during a family argument. Which staging choice is strongest?
options: Increase physical distance from the group while others cluster together
Make everyone stand in an equal straight line
Hide the isolated character behind the set
Ask all actors to speak at the same volume
questions.correctAnswer: Increase physical distance from the group while others cluster together
questions.explanation: Distance and grouping can make emotional separation visible to the audience.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply spatial composition to communicate relationship changes.

questions.prompt: A film edit cuts from a learner beginning to open a door to the same learner entering the room. Which editing technique is being used?
options: Match on action
Jump scare
Curtain speech
Costume plot
questions.correctAnswer: Match on action
questions.explanation: Match on action links continuous movement across separate shots so the cut feels smooth.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply continuity editing vocabulary to shot transitions.

questions.prompt: A dance work about migration needs a clear beginning, development, and ending. Which choreographic plan best fits?
options: Begin with departure, develop travel and conflict, and end with arrival or unresolved searching
Repeat one unrelated gesture with no change
Use only random formations chosen on stage
End before the movement idea is introduced
questions.correctAnswer: Begin with departure, develop travel and conflict, and end with arrival or unresolved searching
questions.explanation: A structured sequence helps the audience follow the dance idea through progression and transformation.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply choreographic structure to communicate a movement idea.

questions.prompt: A stage manager finds two lighting cues with the same cue number in the prompt script. What should happen before rehearsal continues?
options: Renumber and confirm the cues with the lighting operator and director
Ignore the duplicate until performance night
Ask actors to guess when lights should change
Delete all cue notes from the script
questions.correctAnswer: Renumber and confirm the cues with the lighting operator and director
questions.explanation: Accurate cue documentation prevents mistimed or missed technical actions.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply accurate documentation procedures in stage management.

questions.prompt: A performer receives feedback that their character has no clear intention. What should they do first?
options: Identify what the character wants from the other person in each beat
Buy a brighter costume
Speak every line at the same pitch
Remove all pauses from the scene
questions.correctAnswer: Identify what the character wants from the other person in each beat
questions.explanation: Clear intentions turn lines into purposeful action and make relationships easier to read.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply objective analysis to improve scene performance.

questions.prompt: A devised performance has strong individual scenes but feels disconnected. Which rehearsal task should the group use?
options: Map the central idea and create transitions that link scenes through action, sound, or image
Add longer unrelated speeches between all scenes
Remove every repeated image
Let each scene use a different theme without discussion
questions.correctAnswer: Map the central idea and create transitions that link scenes through action, sound, or image
questions.explanation: Transitions and a shared central idea help separate material become one coherent performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply structuring strategies to unify devised performance.

questions.prompt: A public performance poster is being prepared for a school hall event. Which information should be included?
options: Title, date, time, venue, audience guidance, entry details, and contact channel
Only a vague slogan with no event details
Private phone numbers of all cast members
A copied poster from another production
questions.correctAnswer: Title, date, time, venue, audience guidance, entry details, and contact channel
questions.explanation: Responsible publicity gives useful information and avoids privacy or copyright problems.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply clear and ethical publicity practices for performance events.

questions.prompt: A director asks actors to create a frozen image showing unequal power in a meeting. Which technique are they using?
options: Tableau
Voice-over
Montage
Ticketing
questions.correctAnswer: Tableau
questions.explanation: A tableau is a still stage picture that uses bodies, levels, focus, and distance to communicate meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply tableau to communicate dramatic relationships.

questions.prompt: A group wants to show time passing on stage without changing the full set. Which design solution is strongest?
options: Use lighting shifts, sound cues, performer transitions, and selected prop changes
Stop the play for a long explanation after every minute
Replace the entire set after each line
Ignore time changes and hope the audience guesses
questions.correctAnswer: Use lighting shifts, sound cues, performer transitions, and selected prop changes
questions.explanation: Coordinated stagecraft can communicate time economically while keeping performance flow.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply production elements to show changes in time and place.

questions.prompt: A film group wants a shot that reveals a character's loneliness in a crowded corridor. Which option is strongest?
options: Frame the character separated at the edge while others move together in the background
Use only an extreme close-up of a noticeboard
Shake the camera without purpose
Point the camera at the floor during the key moment
questions.correctAnswer: Frame the character separated at the edge while others move together in the background
questions.explanation: Composition can show isolation through placement, contrast, and relationship to surrounding movement.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply framing choices to communicate character state.

questions.prompt: A learner adapts a folktale into a contemporary school setting. Which choice best preserves dramatic strength?
options: Keep the central conflict and moral tension while changing setting, dialogue, and details
Copy the tale word for word with no staging decisions
Remove all conflict to avoid complexity
Add unrelated scenes that do not affect the story
questions.correctAnswer: Keep the central conflict and moral tension while changing setting, dialogue, and details
questions.explanation: Adaptation can transform surface details while retaining the source's core dramatic engine.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply adaptation choices that preserve central conflict and meaning.

questions.prompt: A dance ensemble struggles to enter together after a silent pause. Which rehearsal method best addresses this?
options: Set a shared breath, visual cue, or count that all dancers can follow
Tell each dancer to guess the entry independently
Remove the pause without discussing timing
Ask the audience to clap the entry every time
questions.correctAnswer: Set a shared breath, visual cue, or count that all dancers can follow
questions.explanation: Shared cues help ensemble timing stay precise even when music or sound is minimal.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply rehearsal strategies for synchronised group movement.

questions.prompt: A scene shifts from celebration to danger. Which lighting choice could support the transition safely?
options: Move from bright open light to lower intensity with sharper contrast while keeping exits visible
Turn off all lights so performers cannot see
Keep identical lighting for every mood
Flash lights randomly with no cue or purpose
questions.correctAnswer: Move from bright open light to lower intensity with sharper contrast while keeping exits visible
questions.explanation: Lighting can shift mood while still supporting safety, focus, and visibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply lighting choices to support mood change and performer safety.

questions.prompt: A group is evaluating collaboration after production week. Which evidence is most useful?
options: Attendance, preparation, listening, completed tasks, respectful conduct, and response to feedback
Only the opinion of the loudest performer
Only the colour of the costumes
The number of jokes made backstage
questions.correctAnswer: Attendance, preparation, listening, completed tasks, respectful conduct, and response to feedback
questions.explanation: Collaboration can be judged by observable behaviours that support or weaken production work.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply evidence-based criteria to evaluate production teamwork.

questions.prompt: A film scene needs to show that a decision is private and reflective. Which sound and image choice best supports this?
options: Use quieter ambient sound, a steady close framing, and a pause before the character acts
Add unrelated loud music over every line
Cut rapidly to unrelated objects
Use wide comic movement throughout
questions.correctAnswer: Use quieter ambient sound, a steady close framing, and a pause before the character acts
questions.explanation: Controlled sound, framing, and timing can focus attention on inner thought and choice.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply combined screen elements to communicate reflection.

questions.prompt: A teacher asks learners to turn a health awareness message into theatre for younger pupils. Which approach best fits the audience?
options: Use clear characters, age-appropriate language, realistic choices, and a hopeful action step
Use complex adult legal language throughout
Mock pupils who make mistakes
Avoid showing decisions or consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Use clear characters, age-appropriate language, realistic choices, and a hopeful action step
questions.explanation: Audience-aware theatre communicates serious issues clearly and responsibly without causing confusion or harm.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply audience-appropriate choices when dramatising social issues.

questions.prompt: A performance has a central image of an empty chair. How can the group make the symbol clearer?
options: Repeat and transform the chair's use at key moments connected to absence or authority
Use the chair once randomly and never refer to it again
Hide the chair behind a curtain throughout
Explain the symbol only after the audience leaves
questions.correctAnswer: Repeat and transform the chair's use at key moments connected to absence or authority
questions.explanation: A symbol gains meaning when performance choices connect it consistently to theme and action.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply symbolic repetition to strengthen performance meaning.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to give a useful post-show comment about a dance item. Which comment is most evidence-based?
options: The sudden canon entrance increased tension because each dancer repeated the motif one after another
It was just nice because I liked it
The dance was bad because blue costumes are boring
Everyone should copy a different style next time
questions.correctAnswer: The sudden canon entrance increased tension because each dancer repeated the motif one after another
questions.explanation: Useful critique identifies a specific choice and explains its effect on meaning or audience response.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply evidence-based language to critique choreographic choices.

questions.prompt: A crew must prepare for opening night of a scripted performance. Which checklist is most complete?
options: Rehearsed cues, safe set, checked props, tested sound, confirmed costumes, audience plan, and emergency procedure
Only colourful posters and snacks
Only actor costumes with no technical check
Only the title and cast list
questions.correctAnswer: Rehearsed cues, safe set, checked props, tested sound, confirmed costumes, audience plan, and emergency procedure
questions.explanation: Opening readiness combines artistic, technical, audience, and safety responsibilities.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply comprehensive readiness checks before public performance.

questions.prompt: A performance has impressive costumes, but the audience cannot follow the conflict. What is the strongest analysis?
options: Design choices have not been integrated with clear dramatic action and storytelling
Costumes are the only element that matters in theatre
Audience understanding is never part of performance quality
Actors should ignore plot and focus on fabric
questions.correctAnswer: Design choices have not been integrated with clear dramatic action and storytelling
questions.explanation: Production elements should support the story, theme, relationships, and audience communication.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how design elements support or distract from dramatic communication.

questions.prompt: A short film uses shaky handheld camera movement during a calm interview, distracting viewers from the speaker. What is the best analysis?
options: The camera style conflicts with the interview's intended tone and clarity
Handheld movement is always the most professional choice
The interview would improve if sound became less clear
The subject should move faster to match the camera
questions.correctAnswer: The camera style conflicts with the interview's intended tone and clarity
questions.explanation: Camera style should serve meaning; unnecessary movement can weaken focus and communication.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse whether camera movement supports scene purpose.

questions.prompt: A script begins with conflict, but each later scene repeats the same argument without new stakes or discoveries. What is the main weakness?
options: The plot lacks escalation, development, and changing pressure
The script has too many turning points
The characters change too much in every scene
The ending is over-resolved before the beginning
questions.correctAnswer: The plot lacks escalation, development, and changing pressure
questions.explanation: Drama progresses when information, choices, stakes, and consequences change from scene to scene.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse progression and escalation in dramatic writing.

questions.prompt: A dance item uses high-energy movement for a theme about exhaustion and grief from beginning to end. What is the best critique?
options: The energy quality may contradict the theme unless contrast or intention makes the choice clear
High energy always communicates sadness most clearly
Dance themes do not need movement quality
Slow movement would automatically solve every problem
questions.correctAnswer: The energy quality may contradict the theme unless contrast or intention makes the choice clear
questions.explanation: Movement qualities should be evaluated in relation to theme, contrast, structure, and audience interpretation.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how energy choices support or complicate choreographic meaning.

questions.prompt: A director places the most important conversation at the extreme side of a wide stage while unrelated action continues centre stage. What is the likely problem?
options: Audience focus may be pulled away from the key dialogue
The stage picture automatically becomes clearer
Side placement always increases audibility
Unrelated action always strengthens focus
questions.correctAnswer: Audience focus may be pulled away from the key dialogue
questions.explanation: Focus depends on placement, movement, light, sound, and competing visual information.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how staging choices guide or weaken audience focus.

questions.prompt: A film scene cuts between two characters, but their eyelines suggest they are both looking in the same direction instead of at each other. What issue is most likely?
options: Screen direction and eyeline matching were not controlled across shots
The costumes were too detailed
The scene has too much room tone
The dialogue needs more props
questions.correctAnswer: Screen direction and eyeline matching were not controlled across shots
questions.explanation: Consistent eyelines help viewers understand spatial relationships in edited dialogue scenes.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse screen direction problems in edited scenes.

questions.prompt: A group adapts a sacred community ritual as entertainment without consultation or context. What is the main ethical concern?
options: The work risks cultural misrepresentation and disrespect for community ownership
The performance will automatically become more accurate
Consultation would make creativity impossible
Ethics only applies to film, not theatre
questions.correctAnswer: The work risks cultural misrepresentation and disrespect for community ownership
questions.explanation: Responsible cultural performance requires research, consultation where appropriate, context, and respect.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse ethical risks in representing community performance practices.

questions.prompt: A performer plays anger by shouting every line at the same speed and volume. What is the strongest performance analysis?
options: The emotion lacks variation, tactics, and playable intention, so it may become one-note
Louder acting is always more truthful
Speed alone creates complex characterisation
Anger should never include pauses
questions.correctAnswer: The emotion lacks variation, tactics, and playable intention, so it may become one-note
questions.explanation: Complex acting uses shifts in objective, tactic, pace, silence, focus, and physical detail.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse vocal and physical choices in emotional performance.

questions.prompt: A school documentary includes interview clips but never identifies speakers or the basis of their claims. What is the strongest critique?
options: The documentary weakens credibility because sources and context are unclear
The film becomes more trustworthy when sources are hidden
Interviews never need context in documentary work
Labels would automatically solve all editing issues
questions.correctAnswer: The documentary weakens credibility because sources and context are unclear
questions.explanation: Documentary performance needs transparent context, fair representation, and responsible source handling.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse credibility and context in documentary performance choices.

questions.prompt: A dance ensemble is technically accurate, but every dancer uses the same facial focus and dynamic quality throughout. What is the best analysis?
options: The performance may lack expressive contrast and relationship to the theme
Technical accuracy always guarantees expressive depth
Facial focus is unrelated to dance communication
Variation would automatically make timing inaccurate
questions.correctAnswer: The performance may lack expressive contrast and relationship to the theme
questions.explanation: Strong dance performance combines technical control with expressive dynamics, focus, and intention.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse expressive qualities in dance performance.

questions.prompt: A production spends most of its budget on decoration but leaves no funds for sound equipment needed in a large hall. What is the best analysis?
options: Resource priorities do not match the communication needs of the performance
Decoration is always more important than audibility
Budgets should ignore technical requirements
Sound only matters in film production
questions.correctAnswer: Resource priorities do not match the communication needs of the performance
questions.explanation: A production budget should prioritise choices that make the performance clear, safe, and achievable.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse whether production spending supports performance priorities.

questions.prompt: A devised performance uses a repeated whistle before every scene, but the whistle never connects to character, setting, or theme. What is the strongest critique?
options: The repeated sound lacks clear symbolic or structural purpose
Any repetition automatically creates meaning
Audience members should invent all connections without support
Sound cannot function as a motif
questions.correctAnswer: The repeated sound lacks clear symbolic or structural purpose
questions.explanation: A motif becomes meaningful when repetition is connected to action, theme, emotion, or structure.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the effectiveness of repeated motifs in devised performance.

questions.prompt: A scene is meant to build suspense, but actors rush pauses and reveal information too quickly. What is the best analysis?
options: Pacing and timing weaken tension by not allowing anticipation to develop
Suspense always requires faster delivery
Pauses prevent audiences from understanding plot
The scene needs unrelated comedy to solve the issue
questions.correctAnswer: Pacing and timing weaken tension by not allowing anticipation to develop
questions.explanation: Suspense often depends on controlled timing, withheld information, silence, and delayed response.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how timing choices affect dramatic tension.

questions.prompt: A choreographer uses canon, unison, and counterpoint in one section. What should a Grade 12 analysis focus on?
options: How those relationship devices shape focus, texture, theme, and group meaning
Only whether all dancers wear matching costumes
Whether the audience can count every step aloud
How many minutes the rehearsal took
questions.correctAnswer: How those relationship devices shape focus, texture, theme, and group meaning
questions.explanation: Advanced dance analysis links choreographic devices to meaning, structure, and audience perception.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how group relationship devices affect choreographic meaning.

questions.prompt: A play about corruption ends with every problem solved suddenly by a character who has not appeared before. What is the strongest analysis?
options: The ending may feel unearned because resolution does not grow from established action
Unexpected characters always improve dramatic structure
Resolution should ignore earlier conflict
A sudden ending is automatically realistic
questions.correctAnswer: The ending may feel unearned because resolution does not grow from established action
questions.explanation: A convincing resolution usually develops from prior choices, conflict, pressure, and consequences.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse whether a dramatic resolution is earned by earlier action.

questions.prompt: A performance uses comedy to address bullying, but the jokes mainly ridicule the victim. What is the best ethical analysis?
options: The comic approach risks harm because it shifts sympathy away from the victim and normalises ridicule
Comedy always makes serious topics safer
Ridiculing victims is required for audience engagement
Ethics is irrelevant if the audience laughs
questions.correctAnswer: The comic approach risks harm because it shifts sympathy away from the victim and normalises ridicule
questions.explanation: Responsible performance considers how humour positions people, values, consequences, and audience response.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse ethical implications of humour in performances about social issues.

questions.prompt: A film sequence uses close-ups of hands, cutaways to empty desks, and silence after a character leaves. What should analysis mainly consider?
options: How image selection and sound absence communicate loss or absence
Whether the camera brand is expensive
Whether every shot has the same length
How many people bought tickets
questions.correctAnswer: How image selection and sound absence communicate loss or absence
questions.explanation: Film analysis should connect shot selection, editing, and sound to emotion and meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how visual detail and sound choices create meaning in film.

questions.prompt: A theatre piece uses direct address to ask the audience questions about a community issue. What is the best analysis focus?
options: How breaking the fourth wall positions the audience as participants or witnesses
Whether direct address always removes responsibility
Only whether actors stand at centre stage
How quickly tickets were collected
questions.correctAnswer: How breaking the fourth wall positions the audience as participants or witnesses
questions.explanation: Direct address changes audience relationship by inviting reflection, judgement, or response.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how direct address shapes audience engagement.

questions.prompt: A stage production uses recorded narration to explain every event that actors already show clearly. What is the strongest critique?
options: The narration may be redundant and reduce the impact of performed action
Narration always improves theatre communication
Actors should never communicate through behaviour
Audience members cannot interpret visible action
questions.correctAnswer: The narration may be redundant and reduce the impact of performed action
questions.explanation: Narration should add perspective or structure, not simply repeat what performance already communicates.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse whether narration supports or weakens staged action.

questions.prompt: A final-year production is technically ambitious but has no contingency plan for power failure, performer absence, or rain at an outdoor venue. What is the main weakness?
options: Risk management has not been integrated into production planning
Ambition removes the need for planning
Outdoor performances cannot be prepared safely
Contingency planning is only for professional theatres
questions.correctAnswer: Risk management has not been integrated into production planning
questions.explanation: Production management includes anticipating risks and preparing practical alternatives before presentation.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse gaps in production risk planning.

questions.prompt: A Grade 12 group must create a 12-minute performance on youth unemployment using theatre, dance, and film projection. Which plan is strongest?
options: Develop one central question, assign each medium a clear function, rehearse transitions, and test projection with live action
Create separate unrelated items and join them without transitions
Use projection only because it looks modern
Let each performer decide the theme on opening night
questions.correctAnswer: Develop one central question, assign each medium a clear function, rehearse transitions, and test projection with live action
questions.explanation: Integrated performance needs a shared concept, purposeful media choices, and rehearsed coordination.
questions.learningOutcome: Create an integrated performance plan using theatre, dance, and media elements coherently.

questions.prompt: A director wants to reinterpret a familiar folktale for a modern audience without disrespecting the source. Which approach is best?
options: Research the source, retain core values and conflict, consult where appropriate, and make purposeful contemporary choices
Change names randomly and ignore the story's cultural meaning
Mock traditional characters to seem current
Use the tale without credit because it is old
questions.correctAnswer: Research the source, retain core values and conflict, consult where appropriate, and make purposeful contemporary choices
questions.explanation: Responsible reinterpretation balances creative transformation with knowledge, attribution, and respect.
questions.learningOutcome: Create ethical adaptation strategies for culturally sourced performance material.

questions.prompt: A choreographer must build a solo that later expands into an ensemble section about resilience. Which structure is strongest?
options: Introduce a clear solo motif, vary it through struggle, then let the ensemble share and transform it
Begin with unrelated group movement and never return to the solo idea
Keep the solo and ensemble sections in different themes
Use only symmetrical formations with no development
questions.correctAnswer: Introduce a clear solo motif, vary it through struggle, then let the ensemble share and transform it
questions.explanation: This structure gives the choreography a traceable movement idea that grows from individual to collective meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a choreographic structure that develops motif, theme, and group relationship.

questions.prompt: A film team needs to tell a story about peer pressure with no spoken dialogue. Which plan best uses screen language?
options: Use action, framing, reaction shots, sound, props, and editing rhythm to show choices and consequences
Add long written explanations before every shot
Use random beautiful images unrelated to the situation
Film only a blank wall while music plays
questions.correctAnswer: Use action, framing, reaction shots, sound, props, and editing rhythm to show choices and consequences
questions.explanation: Non-verbal film storytelling depends on visible behaviour, image composition, sound, and editing progression.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a non-dialogue film strategy using screen language.

questions.prompt: A production team has limited money, one classroom, and a large cast. Which design concept is most practical and theatrically strong?
options: Use flexible blocks, actor-created sound, symbolic props, and precise movement to transform the space
Build heavy realistic sets for every location
Cancel design choices because money is limited
Ask the audience to imagine everything with no performance support
questions.correctAnswer: Use flexible blocks, actor-created sound, symbolic props, and precise movement to transform the space
questions.explanation: Low-resource design can be effective when choices are flexible, symbolic, rehearsed, and clearly connected to action.
questions.learningOutcome: Create practical design concepts for limited-resource performance conditions.

questions.prompt: A group must present a performance and also collect audience feedback for improvement. Which evaluation design is strongest?
options: Use focused questions on clarity, engagement, design, and message, then compare responses with rehearsal goals
Ask only whether the audience liked the costumes
Collect comments but never review them
Let performers guess audience response without evidence
questions.correctAnswer: Use focused questions on clarity, engagement, design, and message, then compare responses with rehearsal goals
questions.explanation: Useful evaluation gathers targeted evidence and relates it to the production's intended outcomes.
questions.learningOutcome: Create an audience feedback process for evaluating performance effectiveness.

questions.prompt: A Grade 12 class is producing a community awareness play outdoors. Which production plan is most complete?
options: Confirm permissions, assess weather and sound, plan audience flow, rehearse in the space, prepare backups, and brief the team
Focus only on costumes and ignore the venue
Arrive on the day and decide blocking during the show
Assume outdoor sound and safety will solve themselves
questions.correctAnswer: Confirm permissions, assess weather and sound, plan audience flow, rehearse in the space, prepare backups, and brief the team
questions.explanation: Outdoor production requires permissions, risk checks, technical planning, rehearsal, audience care, and contingencies.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a practical production plan for an outdoor community performance.

questions.prompt: A playwright wants to build a scene where both characters are right from their own point of view. Which writing strategy is strongest?
options: Give each character a clear objective, valid reason, obstacle, and choice that raises the stakes
Make one character obviously foolish from the start
Avoid conflict so neither character struggles
Let both characters explain the theme without action
questions.correctAnswer: Give each character a clear objective, valid reason, obstacle, and choice that raises the stakes
questions.explanation: Complex conflict grows when opposing objectives are understandable and pressure forces meaningful choices.
questions.learningOutcome: Create dramatically balanced conflict through objective, obstacle, and stakes.

questions.prompt: A director must combine live acting with pre-recorded video messages from absent characters. Which rehearsal strategy is strongest?
options: Time the video cues precisely, rehearse actor responses, test visibility and sound, and plan a fallback
Play videos whenever the operator remembers
Let actors ignore the recorded messages
Use video only as decoration unrelated to the scene
questions.correctAnswer: Time the video cues precisely, rehearse actor responses, test visibility and sound, and plan a fallback
questions.explanation: Mixed-media performance succeeds when live and recorded elements interact clearly and reliably.
questions.learningOutcome: Create rehearsal strategies for integrating recorded media with live performance.

questions.prompt: A final performance portfolio must show both artistic quality and responsible process. Which evidence set is strongest?
options: Script drafts, rehearsal notes, design plans, consent records, budget, risk plan, audience feedback, and reflection
Only a cast selfie and the event title
Only ticket sales with no artistic evidence
Only a costume list without process notes
questions.correctAnswer: Script drafts, rehearsal notes, design plans, consent records, budget, risk plan, audience feedback, and reflection
questions.explanation: A strong portfolio documents creative decisions, ethical practice, management, presentation, and learning from evidence.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a portfolio evidence plan for a complete performance production process.
